source: Rast, L. 2008. 'Husbandry and Reproduction', Best Practice Health & Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia, workshop slides (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com)
text: For assessing whether a bull or cow is fit for breeding, the source gives simple physical checklists. Bulls: body condition score 2.5-3, sound feet/legs able to mount, good eyesight with no discharge, healthy teeth/mouth, good coat condition, good temperament, and normal visible reproductive organs (penis, sheath, scrotum, testes) with both testes present, equal size, and good tone on palpation -- scrotal circumference is typically expected to be over 30cm by 2 years of age (less in buffalo), though this varies by breed. Cows: body condition score 2-3, feet/legs/pelvis able to be served and calve, good eyesight, healthy teeth/mouth, good coat, a normal udder with no lumps, no abnormal vulval discharge, no retained placenta, good temperament, and (for older cows) having calved within the last 2 years.
